Nolan Kido / A recorded AI use case

What did AI help change on NolanKido.com?

I used AI to help organize and check pages connecting my practical AI work, technology projects and tournament poker records. The published changes include clearer internal links, evidence-based answers, corrected search metadata and a source-checked video listing. Public release records establish what was published, but search rankings, traffic and AI citations remain unmeasured.

First published within the Technology page on November 3, 2026, expanded on November 5, and moved to this article on November 6. Inspect the original case release. The work applies my AI Works, Human Decides approach to a public publishing task.

November 19, 2026 / 25-turn sprint readout

Did 25 SEO, GEO and AEO improvement turns make this site more visible?

Short answer: the sprint made my published work easier to navigate and verify through named answers, evidence links and tested live pages. It did not establish higher search rankings, more Google impressions, more clicks, or additional AI-answer citations. A release check tells me what readers can reach; search and assistant observations are needed to show what they did find.

November 21 follow-up: The 224-to-225 URL table below describes November 19, not today's inventory. The live sitemap now lists 230 URLs. Public checks also found the written 10 BB guide, workflow pilot, and recorded editing case reachable through recent site changes (release record). None measures indexing, Google impressions, visits, or AI citations.

What actually changed? The source-linked Nolan Kido identity answer and NolanPoker and AI evidence bridge clarify authorship. The Google search-advice audit and fictional AI poker claim check expose how a recommendation can be tested. The reproducible tournament solver-fit example gives readers the underlying conditions and calculations. The 25-turn evidence ledger separates these published changes from observations that have not been collected.

What measurement would actually test the result?

  1. Establish comparable search periods. Use the existing free Search Console export procedure and offline CSV checker. October 2026 is before this November 17 to 19 sprint; November mixes before-and-after days; December is the first full month afterward. Wait for each reporting period to close and settle before comparing, and keep the original exports private.
  2. Measure AI features separately. Review Google's generative AI performance report if it is available for the verified property, and record assistant referrals or Bing citations only when their original provider reports are accessible. Do not add Google AI impressions to the overall Web impressions, where that activity is already included.
  3. Keep the question panel unchanged. Run the same twenty nonbranded and five branded questions in recorded assistant/search modes, verifying actual clickable citations. The first completed run is a post-sprint baseline, not proof of improvement, because no comparable presprint answer observations were captured.
  4. Choose the next edit from evidence. Fix confirmed indexing or canonical problems first. For pages with observed impressions but weak click-through, inspect query intent and snippet fit. For real assistant answers that omit a useful page, check whether its facts and internal links answer the question. Recheck after changes; do not assign causation to one release based on an unmatched period.

Boundary: all public sprint reports document the work performed, but not every turn introduced a new URL or a separate deployment. No subscription, private analytics upload, crawler-access bypass, new AI markup or background monitor is required to follow this method. Actual searches, assistant answers and user outcomes remain subject to later observation.

November 18, 2026 / A current worked example

How can I verify an AI-assisted website change actually went live?

Short answer: verify the original source, the intended page change, the local release checks and the exact public response as four separate steps. Then measure search and AI-answer discovery separately. I used this method on NolanKido.com when a public NolanPoker video title and thumbnail changed. The result was a documented publication, not a claimed SEO win.

What happened in the November 18 Reserve video update?

  1. Check the primary source. The public YouTube oEmbed listing used the title My Ace-King Reshove in a 3-Way All-In | WSOP Circuit. The public thumbnail had changed too. The dated public evidence ledger records the earlier and newer listing titles and the thumbnail hash. Neither metadata nor an illustration verifies the video's spoken content or cards.
  2. Compare what the site says. The Poker hub, player profile and Reserve Day 1 companion now use the reviewed listing and separate links to the source-bounded main- and side-pot explanation. The merged pull request #386 makes the exact changes inspectable; it did not create a duplicate article URL.
  3. Run bounded checks. The offline listing checker compares title, video identity, source text and saved JPEG against the ledger. Synthetic negative controls reject stale or invented matches. The recorded local release generated 253 files without drift, checked 225 sitemap URLs, parsed 230 HTML pages and found zero issues among 16,240 internal links. These checks cannot validate the current video's footage or a search engine's index.
  4. Inspect public bytes after merging. After the change reached the main branch, direct read-only GETs matched the committed public files for five destinations: the Poker hub, player profile, Reserve companion, stored thumbnail and public ledger. A byte match at that moment confirms the intended files were served, not permanent uptime, ranking gains or a complete browser-accessibility review.

Can a site owner repeat this check? Yes. Inspect the public pull request and dated release record, run the offline checker on a copy of the public repository and compare the published files with the same paths in that checkout. The checker's optional --live mode makes two public, read-only requests to detect a later YouTube listing change; it does not inspect the video's audio. Exact public bytes can change after another legitimate release, so compare against the matching revision, not an arbitrary older checkout.

Did this prove better Google rankings or more ChatGPT citations?

No. The evidence establishes an updated and publicly served page, not more clicks, impressions, positions, AI-answer links or subscriptions. The connected search-data service was unavailable without a paid subscription, which I did not start. For follow-up, use the free monthly Search Console export method and separate AI-answer citation sample below. Missing data is unavailable, not zero.

Before accepting a recommendation to add special AI-search markup, compare the claim with Google's actual AI Overviews requirements. A publication receipt and search eligibility are distinct from a measured citation.

This is my own site's AI-assisted publishing case, not a client engagement or an independent search-performance experiment. The public evidence is limited to source metadata, committed site files and the stated release checks; the present YouTube cut was not independently reviewed from a complete transcript.

A public release trail / What the evidence supports

Five website changes with public sources.

  1. Link to the work. Home and About gained routes to the local-AI laptop guide and reply-audit case; Home also linked my tournament player record. Inspect the link changes.
  2. Correct freshness dates. Four landing pages' sitemap lastmod dates were aligned with substantive revisions, without treating a rebuild as publication. Inspect the sitemap correction.
  3. Answer a practical question. The small-business AI pilot guide sets task boundaries, review ownership and stop conditions. It is guidance, not a claimed client deployment. Inspect the published change.
  4. Surface supporting evidence. Home gained examples of accounting research, practical AI work and tournament records, plus a Check the evidence shortcut near its primary action. Inspect the cards and shortcut.
  5. Connect creator work. The Poker video index and player profile expanded from three to five owner-supplied public video links, distinct from two older written companions. A direct NolanPoker channel link followed. Inspect video discovery and the channel route. The site did not infer current-cut titles, hand histories or timestamps.

What the evidence made me leave out

The identity-data correction removed claims lacking reviewed public support. Poker updates linked actual uploads without inventing their contents. The work also respected the owner's restrictions on authored GitHub Actions and paid search services. These choices are not a claim that AI output was independently reviewed by every person affected.

The missing outcome measurement

Not established: increased impressions, clicks, rankings, indexing, reader satisfaction, YouTube subscriptions or AI-answer inclusion. Those outcomes need baseline and follow-up measurements with consistent definitions. Publication checks alone do not establish them.

A no-cost monthly check: An offline Search Console CSV summarizer turns owner-exported page, query and optional daily chart reports into a private aggregate JSON summary. The export and interpretation instructions explain the missing-data rules. With a complete daily chart export, it checks calendar coverage and uses chart rows for property clicks and impressions, never a sum of truncated page rows. It makes no network calls, does not expose query text in the output, and cannot confirm the original Search Console filters, freshness, or the date ranges of separate table exports.

How to check search visibility without paying for another dashboard

A website can pass technical checks and still have no measured search improvement. A useful follow-up compares the same reporting period and filters over time, without treating page publication as proof of more clicks. Here is a free procedure that keeps the raw data on your computer.

  1. Export one complete month. In your verified Google Search Console property, open Search results, select Web and the last complete calendar month, then export the daily chart (sometimes Dates.csv) and Pages table. Record the property, date range, filters and export date privately. Queries are optional.
  2. Run the local checker. Save the Python script linked above beside the CSV files. In that folder, this example handles a month-first chart dated like 10/1/2026: 
    py -3 .\gsc-monthly-local-audit.py --month 2026-10 --pages .\Pages.csv --chart .\Dates.csv --chart-date-format mdy
  3. Read the two kinds of totals separately. Property clicks and impressions appear only when the daily chart has every date in the selected month. The Technology, Poker and other section totals are sums of the exported Pages rows, which may be limited. A visible nonbrand Technology click lower bound requires a combined Query + Page export, never a join of separate files. For ISO chart dates, omit the format option; use dmy for explicitly day-first dates.
  4. Repeat without overclaiming. Use the same property, Search type and filters for a later complete month. Check the figures against Search Console before keeping a private scorecard. A month-over-month difference does not establish causation, indexing, AI-generated citations or reader satisfaction.

Try it before exporting private data. Download the synthetic Pages CSV and synthetic Dates CSV. Both contain invented counts, with an extra Synthetic column marked YES. Save the two files beside the Python checker, then run this Windows command:

py -3 .\gsc-monthly-local-audit.py --month 2026-10 --pages .\gsc-synthetic-pages.csv --chart .\gsc-synthetic-dates.csv --chart-date-format mdy

Expected fictional result: 31 October dates, 62 property clicks and 3,100 property impressions from the sample chart, versus 22 clicks across the three sample Pages rows (12 Technology, 7 Poker, 3 Other). The gap is intentional: page-row totals cannot stand in for property totals. Optional query figures remain unavailable because no query file is supplied. These files are not genuine Google exports, Nolan Kido traffic measurements or evidence of SEO growth. This release of the checker recognizes nolankido.com URLs and its section names are specific to this site; using it for another website requires adapting those rules. The checker still prints its standard privacy warning because real exports must stay private.

Google explains the property-versus-page counting distinction and export row limits. The open-source tool's initial release, daily-chart validation and explicit date formats are inspectable changes, not observed search gains. The script prints aggregate JSON locally, writes no file on its own and never sends your CSV data away.

A method you can reuse: name a reader's question, identify the best existing page, make a useful and accurately linked revision, preserve its canonical URL, verify the published result, and measure the outcome separately. Google's link guidance explains crawlable descriptive links; its sitemap guidance explains when a changed date is meaningful. Neither promises a ranking increase.

How to measure AI-search citations without treating them as search clicks

A site can appear in an AI-generated answer without receiving a visit, and a cited page is not necessarily a high-ranking ordinary search result. Four separate measurements help keep the claim honest. Download a blank monthly AI-search observation worksheet, or read the complete public measurement protocol. Keep completed records private.

Which source measures which part of discovery
SourceWhat it can measureWhat it does not establish
Google Search Console, WebOverall organic clicks and impressions in Google Search for the selected site, dates and filters, including AI feature activity that is part of the overall report.How many chatbot answers mentioned the site.
Search Console, Generative AI performance (Search)A dedicated view of impressions in Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, already included in overall Search reporting.Exact cited links in ChatGPT or the number of visits. An absent report is not a confirmed zero.
Bing Webmaster Tools, AI PerformanceAggregated visible citation activity and cited pages across supported Microsoft AI experiences.ChatGPT-wide citations, clicks, rankings, or an exhaustive log of individual answers.
Own analytics and a fixed assistant prompt panelVisits with recognized assistant referrers, and actual clickable links found in a small manually repeated answer sample.All assistant-driven visits or a universal citation rate. Referrer information and answer samples can be incomplete.

A repeatable no-cost monthly check

  1. Fix the scope first. Use the last complete calendar month, note the search property and filters, and keep a fixed panel of unbranded practical questions. Do not replace the panel each month with prompts designed to produce a favorable response.
  2. Read the first-party reports separately. Record Google Web clicks, the dedicated Google generative AI Search impression view when available, and Bing's AI Performance citations. The AI-impression view overlaps with overall Google Search performance. Preserve each provider's date range and coverage; do not add these figures together.
  3. Check traffic separately. Look for recognized assistant referral domains or campaign parameters in your own analytics, if available. Missing referrer data cannot prove that no AI-assisted visits occurred.
  4. Sample actual answers. Run each fixed prompt in a new search-enabled conversation, record the product and mode, and count a trial as cited only when the completed answer includes a genuine clickable link to the domain. A text-only mention, search snippet, or URL you supplied in the prompt is not a verified citation. Count each completed trial at most once.
  5. Compare without inventing causality. Save exact dates, completed-trial denominators, and the original page URLs privately. A before-and-after change could reflect demand, search systems, competitors or sampling variation, not only your latest article.

Check your completed citation panel without uploading it

For a reproducible count, download the blank CSV trial log, the offline citation checker (Python), and the explicitly fictional 16-trial example. These are free text files; the checker uses only Python's standard library and makes no network calls.

  1. Record a genuine trial. Put a single row in your private CSV for each of the eight unbranded prompts and each planned assistant and search mode. Record the observation date, assistant, mode and whether the answer completed. Use clickable_link_verified=yes only after a person has inspected a real clickable link to this domain in the completed answer. The checker validates its URL format, but cannot independently prove what the assistant displayed.
  2. Run the checker privately. Keep your completed CSV, screenshots and prompt records outside this public repository. Save all three sample downloads in one folder, then use the fictional example to test the method before adding your own observations:
py -3 .\ai-citation-panel-audit.py --month 2026-10 --expected-trials 16 --csv .\ai-citation-panel-synthetic.csv

Expected fictional result: two manually marked clickable-link trials out of 16 completed trials, or 12.5%, plus one separate text-only mention. The result is intentionally synthetic, not this site's measured visibility. With fewer completed trials, the denominator shrinks and the report states how much of the panel is missing. If none completed, the percentage is null, not zero. Duplicate trials, spoofed domains and conflicting citation flags are rejected.

For a private real panel, replace the synthetic CSV path and month with your own observed file and date range. Set --expected-trials to eight times the number of planned assistant/mode combinations, such as 16 for two. The checker prints aggregate JSON and does not include raw URLs, run a chatbot, visit a link or write any file. The optional evidence notes and exact response links remain yours to keep privately. Do not treat partial coverage as a complete evaluation.

Fictional interpretation: If two of 16 completed answer trials contain a clickable domain link, the observed sample fraction is 2/16, or 12.5%. It is not a platform-wide citation rate. Seven reported Bing citations would remain a separate provider metric, and a missing Google AI report would be recorded as unavailable, not zero.

How can I test whether AI answers cite my site across different topics?

Freeze the questions before testing, verify each actual link, and score branded and nonbranded answers separately. I published a fixed 25-question sprint panel (.csv) on November 17, 2026: twenty questions ask about practical AI or tournament poker without naming me, and five name Nolan Kido. Every prompt has a predetermined relevant page. The original frozen method states how to run it. A nonbranded response that merely repeats my name after I supplied my site would not test discovery.

Use the blank observation log (.csv) and offline 25-prompt audit (.py). For every prompt and preselected assistant/search mode, start a fresh conversation, use the exact prompt without introducing this site, keep the raw answer privately, and verify any genuinely clickable first-party citation. If several first-party links appear, log the expected page when it was among them; otherwise log another cited page. Mark the answer's correctness and whether it completed the user's task by human inspection. A link to another page on this site is not the same as citing the expected answer page.

Keep the two public panels distinct: the eight unbranded questions and older checker above form a shorter monthly check. This twenty-five-question sprint panel is a separate frozen baseline, with twenty nonbranded and five branded prompts. Do not pool their counts or call one a before-and-after result for the other.

Download all three 25-prompt files to one private folder. A Windows PowerShell example using the blank log is:

py -3 .\ai-answer-sprint-25-audit.py --month 2026-11 --expected-modes 2 --prompts .\ai-answer-sprint-25-prompts.csv --csv .\ai-answer-sprint-25-blank.csv

Expected result from the empty template: fifty planned trials, zero completed, fifty missing, and sample_fraction: null for both segments. This is a missing-data example, not an observation that no assistant cited the site. For real trials, use your actual month and private log with one row per prompt and assistant/mode. The script refuses an altered prompt file, duplicate trials and lookalike domains; it checks labels and URL syntax but cannot independently verify that an assistant really returned the link. It prints only aggregate JSON and makes no network calls.

No AI-answer trials, Search Console impressions, rankings or assistant referrals were measured in this site revision. A blocked paid search connector does not change that boundary. Completed answer text, screenshots, prompt results, private analytics and personal information must stay outside the public repository. Repeating the same panel later can describe a bounded sample under recorded settings, not a platform-wide recommendation rate or a causal SEO gain.

Crawler eligibility is separate from being cited: OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot guidance explains how search crawling can be allowed independently of GPTBot training controls. Allowing discovery does not guarantee an answer link. The worksheet and this method make no claim that nolankido.com has already gained ChatGPT citations or increased traffic.

This is a source-linked account of work on my own public site, prepared with AI assistance. It is not a client case study, paid search experiment, independently validated SEO result, or endorsement from a search provider.
